claim_scope: Current local campaign inputs and configured repository behavior only; no independent source-clock, provider, license, or authoritative session-calendar claim.

timestamp_contract.tick_localization_behavior: Parse source date/time as naive wall-clock labels and localize with the configured fixed-offset carrier. TickBook retains stable source-row order for equal timestamps.
timestamp_contract.session_feature_behavior: The configured FTMO model maps source wall labels to New York wall time by subtracting seven hours, then localizes with America/New_York. Ambiguous or nonexistent reconstructed labels raise instead of being guessed.
timestamp_contract.verification_boundary: These are configured code semantics. The available local export does not independently authenticate its source timezone, UTC offset, or DST policy.

observed_local_quote_facts.quote_side_availability_interpretation: The bid and ask may be carried from separate source rows; the resulting pair does not prove simultaneous quote availability.

bar_availability_facts.availability_rule: A derived aggregate is exposed only at its configured or nominal close boundary and first appears on the first observed M1 row at or after that boundary.
bar_availability_facts.limitation: Partial bins are descriptive and are not classified as data loss, closures, or schedule gaps.

bounded_no_go: Do not interpret source-row order within millisecond timestamp ties as true sub-millisecond market chronology.
Do not claim that carried bid and ask values were simultaneously available.
Do not assert an authoritative timezone, DST transition, or session calendar from repository configuration alone.
Do not make provider, license, or external-calendar claims; those topics are outside the user-authorized local-data scope.
limitations: No raw market data is copied into this packet.
Counts describe the hash-identified selected campaign exports; they are not universal feed properties.
This packet narrows local timestamp and quote claims but does not establish executable policy value or simulator parity.
